scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for Pokemon Song Best Collection and six rows that show CD-insert reprint context, music-media assembly, and language/variant traps.
in_scope: Pokemon Song Best Collection release dossier

context.name_ja: ポケモンソング・ベストコレクション

sources.title: Local Japanese pre-English release catalog: Pokemon Song Best Collection
Selected local snapshot: Computer Error glossy Song Best versus Kamex print boundary

claims.text: The local catalog models Pokemon Song Best Collection as a January 1, 1999 CD insert/reprint promo product-family row.
The local catalog and Bulbapedia model Pokemon Song Best Collection as eleven included cards.
Bulbapedia describes Pokemon Song Best Collection as a music CD product and says the cards included with it had all been previously released through other Japanese promotions.
The local catalog's attention rows include Venusaur, Charizard, Blastoise, Mewtwo, Mew, Cool Porygon, Hungry Snorlax, Computer Error, Super Energy Retrieval, and an English Pikachu inclusion.
Bulbapedia and the selected local Kamex snapshot distinguish the glossy CoroCoro/Song Best Collection Computer Error lane from a later non-glossy Kamex Mega Battle participation print.
The local catalog's credited artists for the eleven included rows include Mitsuhiro Arita, Ken Sugimori, Christopher Rush, Hiromichi Sugiyama, Sumiyoshi Kizuki, and Keiji Kinebuchi.

Pokemon Song Best Collection matters because it turns cards into an appendix of Pokemon's media assembly: music, campaigns, earlier promos, Japanese CD packaging, and one English card all meet in one product object.

not_claiming: first distribution for each included card
steps: Treat this as a CD-included product-context slice, not a normal booster set and not first-distribution proof for the included cards.
Preserve the row's Song Best membership claim separately from any earlier promo, campaign, or set-print claim.
For each card, ask whether the seller is claiming a Song Best CD copy, an earlier promo copy, or only the same artwork/card name.
Treat local symbol status as mixed product context, not Japanese Base No Rarity proof.
For Pikachu 011, preserve the row-level language caveat: the included card is English inside a Japanese CD product.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Song Best Collection is a media-product reprint context; CD inclusion, earlier promotion, language, and variant lane must not be collapsed.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, or binder import says Song Best, CD promo, Japanese CD, unnumbered promo, or names one of the included cards without distribution context.

narrative.human_title: The soundtrack becomes a card binder
narrative.why_it_matters: Pokemon Song Best Collection is one of those objects that makes the franchise feel assembled by many hands at once. It is a music CD, but tucked inside is a little card-memory cabinet: starters, mythics, Nintendo 64 campaign oddities, Computer Error, and even an English Pikachu. The joy is not that it behaves like a normal set. The joy is that it does not. It shows Pokemon becoming media infrastructure, where songs, promotions, campaigns, and cards all point back at the same growing world.

narrative.human_title: The grass starter as media memory
narrative.why_it_matters: Venusaur in Song Best feels like a founding image being placed into a scrapbook. Mitsuhiro Arita's early-card memory is doing the work here: the CD does not need to explain why Venusaur matters. It assumes the listener already knows, then lets the card sit beside the songs as proof that Pokemon had become a whole childhood apparatus.

sources.title: Bulbapedia: Pikachu (Base Set 58)
not_claiming: Song Best copy in seller possession

claims.text: The local catalog identifies row 011 as Pikachu / ピカチュウ in Pokemon Song Best Collection and carries a language caveat that the included card is English inside a Japanese CD product.
The local catalog credits the Song Best Pikachu row to Mitsuhiro Arita.
The local catalog and Bulbapedia page link this Song Best membership row to the English Base Set Pikachu card rather than to a Japanese-language Pikachu promo.

Pikachu matters here because it is the row that breaks the lazy rule: a Japanese CD product can contain an English card, so an agent has to preserve language as part of identity rather than treating country-of-product as language-of-card.

steps: Preserve the row-level language caveat: this is an English Base Set Pikachu card included in a Japanese CD product.
Do not route this row as a Japanese-language Pikachu promo without explicit contrary evidence.
Record Mitsuhiro Arita as the local illustrator credit, but do not use artist credit alone as a physical-card identifier.
Ask for packaging and card-language evidence if a seller claims a Song Best Pikachu.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Pikachu 011 is the language-boundary trap: Japanese product context does not mean Japanese printed card.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want says Song Best Pikachu, Japanese CD Pikachu, Japanese Pikachu, or Base Pikachu in CD context.

narrative.human_title: The mascot proves language is part of identity
narrative.why_it_matters: Pikachu is the card that makes the agent slow down. It is in a Japanese CD product, but the catalog carries the English-card caveat. That little mismatch is beautiful protocol material: the mascot is familiar, the product is Japanese, the card language is English, and only careful assembly keeps those facts from collapsing into one sloppy label.
